Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 120, English)
Ashaeiynn: A Guided "Screen" Vision — One Devotee's Journey Through the Havan, Surya Lok, and Mata's Blessings

This transcript has no fr esh "welcome" opening — it begins dir ectly with Bhaiya guiding a devotee (addr essed as "behan," sister) into a live divya-drishti ("divine sight") vision, narrated by her in r eal time over r oughly 40 minutes while he pr ompts her along. Its format (one uninterrupted individual vision narration, rather than a case-study lectur e or a gr oup ritual) is a drastic shift fr om Session 1 19's Christmas Day case study , so it is tr eated as its own, separate session. This document r ecor ds the devotee's narrated vision, and Bhaiya's guiding pr ompts, exactly as given — strictly as a documentary account of this teaching's own devotional/visionary tradition, not as independently verified fact, and not as a technique guide for a r eader to r eplicate. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document.
Part A — Setup: Being Guided Into the "Scr een"

1. How the vision is framed at the outset: Bhaiya tells the devotee that because she has "called upon the screen" and honored Ashaeiynn's guru lineage and its word, she has been granted access to "Ashaeiynn's screen" — she is instructed to keep her eyes closed for 30–40 minutes and to narrate everything she sees or feels as it happens, while he (and, in this teaching's framing, "Baba") guides her through it.
2. The devotee's opening prayer: She is told to mentally ask her guru to begin the process, then to report what begins appearing.
Part B — The Vision: A Ritual/Havan Space

1. A goddess figur e performing healing: The devotee describes a goddess in a red saree, crowned, holding a trishul (trident), performing what she describes as a healing process specifically for those present who are connected to a kuldevi (family goddess) or another form of the divine mother .
2. Hanuman ji Maharaj's pr esence: Two tall forms of Hanuman ji Maharaj are described standing behind "Bhaiya" in the vision, though only partially visible.

3. The havan kund (fir e-altar) and its portal: A colored yantra is described inside the havan kund, with a portal beneath it connected to multiple distinct ener gies conver ging there; devotees performing pheri (circling) around it are described as forming a bandhan (bond/protective link) as they circle.

4. Negativity being drawn out and worked on: The devotee describes doots standing to the side drawing negativity , malinta (impurity), or pitru-related influence up and out of anyone who has it, bringing it before "Bhaiya" for it to be addressed there.

5. Individual pr otective "rings": Everyone present is described as encircled by a ring-shaped protective boundary , each connected to their own individual ener gy portal — described as functioning as a personal protective shield, continuously fed by
golden ener gy from Bhaiya's own hand as he places it on people's heads.

6. Other deities present in the vision: Bholenath (Shiva) providing calming ener gy to those whose ener gy had become intense; Dur ga Mata weaving a protective bond; a Bhairav tattva; a Kali Mata's attendant doot working on dif ferent individuals; Sheshnag behind Bhaiya; and — noted explicitly by the devotee as a first-time sighting — a form she identifies as "Ramapir ji" (a real, traditionally venerated folk deity), whom she is guided to bow to.

7. A large pr otective boundary: The devotee describes everyone present as encircled by a lar ge, continuous protective boundary ("like a cage," in her words) with ener gy raining down from above, which she says nothing from outside could penetrate.

8. A canopy of flowers, and the Ram Darbar: An umbrella-like canopy is described showering flowers over Bhaiya; a vision of the Ram Darbar (Ram, Sita, and attendants) is described seated immediately beside the havan kund, with Hanuman ji at their feet and saints receiving blessings from them; Sage Valmiki is also described as visible.

9. The central energy sour ce: A kalash (ritual pot) with a coconut and leaves at the center of the havan kund is described as the main visible source of the ener gy in the vision, dif ferentiated by color (gold-glitter , blue, pink) depending, per the devotee's account, on what kind of tattva a given person is receiving; water is also described as visible inside the kund.
10. Weapons and symbols visible in the havan kund: A trishul, damroo (small drum), shankh (conch), and a spear (bhala) are described inside the kund, along with a torch with visible flame.

1 1. A vision of Ram ji in his for est-exile (vanvasi) form , and a lar ge, guardian-like entity (described by the devotee as lion-like) associated with the pillars around the havan kund, identified as a fierce-natured doot assigned to that role.
12. How negativity is described as being drawn upward in this vision: Via a trishul, used (per the devotee's description) to pull negativity up and out of those af fected.
Part C — The Journey Onward: Gates, Stairs, and Surya Lok

1. A rapid journey thr ough a narr ow path: The devotee describes being taken quickly along a single, enclosed path (which she compares to a pipe), told simply to keep watching and reporting what she sees.
2. A gate, and a spiral stair case: An open gate is described, followed by a spiral staircase leading upward, past many saints and doots serving as guards.

3. A large hall, a number ed badge, and an exchange of "tattva": The devotee describes being led into a lar ge hall resembling an event venue, given a badge reading "Ashaeiynn 32" (or a similar number) and told where to sit; she describes some of her own tattva being removed and new tattva being added, and weapons/astras displayed nearby being explained to her .

4. Arrival at Surya Lok, per this teaching: In response to Bhaiya's question, the devotee identifies the realm she has arrived at as Surya Lok (the realm of the Sun deity); she reports being unable to see Surya Bhagwan directly due to the intensity of the light, and describes an ID-card check taking place before devotees could approach further , receiving a blessing from a distance instead.

5. A check-in exchange: Bhaiya asks the devotee her name and where she is from, as a routine check that she remains present and aware during the narration — a practice consistent with how this project's other guided-vision sessions confirm the devotee's continued engagement.

6. Celebration and prasad: The devotee describes applause, drums (dhol), and a line where prasad (a golden, glittering substance she describes as itself carrying a tattva) is distributed; a havan kund with several saints performing continuous havan is described as generating light so intense that further detail becomes hard to make out.
Part D — Transformation and a Further Realm

1. Seeing herself as a child: The devotee describes seeing her own form as that of a small child; Bhaiya explains this, in this teaching's own framing, as a natural relative ef fect of being in the presence of much lar ger/more senior subtle beings — not a literal transformation.

2. Continued rapid travel, arrival at a new r ealm: The devotee describes traveling at high speed through white light to a rocky , mountainous location, then an old-style gate from which many doots emer ge in a line, joining a procession of numerous saints performing japa.

3. A purification pond (kund/sar ovar): Saints in white robes with tripund (a traditional Shaiva forehead marking) are described guiding her to a pond meant for purifying the subtle body — described in this teaching as a process in which doshas and negative elements remain behind in the water while a new , purified subtle body emer ges; this occurs alongside a traditional devotional bhajan playing about wielding a gada (mace) to protect devotees.
Part E — A Realm of Individual Healing, Identified as Possibly Ashaeiynn's Own

1. The devotee's own tentative identification: She suggests this may be a realm belonging specifically to Ashaeiynn, where each devotee's subtle body receives individualized attention for whatever issue it carries, while devotees without such issues are shown seated in a saint-like posture, performing japa.
2. The described process: Bandhan (binding attachments) are cut first, after which devotees are shown gaining access to protection and to an ongoing "ener gy access."

3. A vision of Parikshit Bhaiya and "Baba": The devotee describes Parikshit Bhaiya seated on/above a throne-like seat, elevated roughly three feet in the air , performing japa; behind him, a lar ge form in white she identifies as "Baba," visible only up to a certain point due to the intensity of devotion/ener gy around him. Ram Bhagwan, the Ram family , and Sita Mata are described as present, with Sita Mata radiating blessing to everyone, and a circle of deities surrounding all the assembled subtle bodies, continuously channeling ener gy to them.

4. Multiple subtle bodies performing differ ent tasks simultaneously: The devotee describes some individuals as having more than one subtle body present at once (she notes seeing as many as three for a single person), each engaged in a dif ferent activity — one performing japa, another of fering water to Shiva, another performing seva (service).

5. A bound ar ea for negativity/pitru-r elated entities: The devotee describes a net-like enclosed area where bound negativity and pitru-related entities are held, with Baba's doots disciplining them there; she also describes a subset of that same bound group attempting to perform japa in a separate section within the enclosure, describing this as those entities receiving both discipline and an opportunity at the same time. This is recorded here strictly as a description of the devotee's own reported vision, consistent with similar devotional/cosmological imagery already documented elsewhere in this project — not as a literal claim about the treatment of any real being.
Part F — A Palace, Further Gates, and Individual Gifts Fr om Mata

1. A palace and garden, traveled alone: The devotee describes arriving, this time without an escorting doot, at what she describes as a lar ge palace with a colorful garden, ascending connecting spiral stairways, passing through a hall with food/of ferings laid out, and a further hall where puja (tilak, aarti) was being performed.

2. A Shivalay (Shiva shrine), and a hall of only Mata's feet: She describes passing a Shiva shrine lit with many lamps, then arriving at a hall where only Mata's glowing feet are visible (her full form is not, due to the intensity of the devotion/ener gy present); she is told simply to bow , and that whatever Mata wishes to give will be received there.

3. Gifts described as r eceived in the vision: A "chain" placed through her body , said to close a subtle portal that had existed there; two portals continuously supplying golden ener gy to what she identifies as her eight subtle bodies; a shield and a trishul; a small crown-like object from Mata; an "agni jyot" (flame), which Mata is described as saying will always signify her presence whenever it is seen; an unspecified "vidya" (mystical knowledge/capacity); a rotating shield weapon connected to a rod, described as able to deflect anything approaching; a sighting of Raghunath ji's (Ram's) sandals (charan paduka); and a large, box-shaped "vidya" received near the vision's end.

4. How the vision ends: A portal is described opening, through which the devotee is led back; the narration closes with Parikshit Bhaiya appearing to do something at her head, and the transcript ends mid-sentence, consistent with a recording cut.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This document r ecords one devotee's guided, first-person divya-drishti ("divine sight") vision, narrated live over roughly 40 minutes with Bhaiya's pr ompting — presented strictly as a documentary account of this teaching's own devotional/visionary tradition, not as independently verified fact. The vision moves thr ough a havan/ritual space (with healing, pr otective "rings," and negativity being drawn out and worked on), then thr ough a sequence of gates, stairs, and r ealms (including Surya Lok and a further purification pond), to a r ealm the devotee tentatively identifies as possibly Ashaeiynn's own , and finally to an encounter with Mata, from whom she describes receiving several symbolic gifts. This teaching frames "seeing oneself as smaller/younger" in the pr esence of senior subtle beings as a natural r elative effect within the vision , not a literal claim about the devotee's real age or body . Real, traditionally venerated figur es referenced in this vision (Ramapir ji, Sage Valmiki, Ram Darbar) ar e presented factually and r espectfully , consistent with traditional devotional practice. This document is not a technique guide — it does not instruct a reader on how to "open a screen," summon a vision, or replicate any part of this experience; see the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 120, English)
Ashaeiynn: A Guided "Screen" Vision — One Devotee's Journey Through the Havan, Surya Lok, and Mata's Blessings

Q1. How does this guided vision session begin? A1. Bhaiya tells the devotee she has been granted access to "Ashaeiynn's screen" because she called upon it and honored the guru lineage's word; she is told to keep her eyes closed for 30–40 minutes and narrate everything she sees or feels as it happens.

Q2. What does the devotee first describe seeing? A2. A goddess figure in a red saree, crowned, holding a trishul, performing a healing process for those connected to a kuldevi (family goddess) or another divine-mother form, alongside two tall, partially visible forms of Hanuman ji Maharaj.

Q3. What does she describe happening at the havan kund? A3. A colored yantra with a portal beneath it connected to multiple ener gies; devotees circling it (pheri) forming a protective bond (bandhan) as they go; doots drawing negativity and pitru-related influence out of those who have it and bringing it forward.

Q4. What pr otective imagery does she describe for those pr esent? A4. Everyone encircled by an individual ring-shaped protective boundary connected to their own ener gy portal, fed continuously by golden ener gy from Bhaiya's hand, and a lar ger , cage-like protective boundary around the whole group.

Q5. Which other deities and figur es appear in this part of the vision? A5. Bholenath (Shiva) calming intense ener gy in some devotees; Dur ga Mata weaving protection; a Bhairav tattva; a Kali Mata doot; Sheshnag; the Ram Darbar seated beside the havan kund with Hanuman ji at their feet; Sage Valmiki; and, seen for the first time in this teaching's account, a form identified as "Ramapir ji," a traditionally venerated folk deity .

Q6. What does she describe as the central energy sour ce in the havan kund? A6. A kalash (ritual pot) with a coconut and leaves, generating dif ferently colored ener gy (gold-glitter , blue, pink) depending on what each person is receiving, alongside weapons and symbols (trishul, damroo, shankh, spear , a lit torch) also visible inside the kund.
Q7. How does she describe negativity being r emoved in this vision? A7. Via a trishul, used to pull negativity up and out of those affected.

Q8. What happens after the havan-space portion of the vision? A8. The devotee is taken rapidly along a narrow , enclosed path (compared to a pipe) to a gate, then up a spiral staircase past saints and guarding doots, into a lar ge hall where she is given a numbered badge ("Ashaeiynn 32" or similar) and told where to sit, with some of her own tattva reportedly exchanged.

Q9. What r ealm does the devotee say she r eaches next? A9. Surya Lok (the realm of the Sun deity), confirmed in response to Bhaiya's question — she describes being unable to see Surya Bhagwan directly due to the intensity of the light, an ID-card check before approaching further , and receiving blessing from a distance.

Q10. Why does Bhaiya ask her name and wher e she's from mid-vision? A10. As a routine check-in to confirm she remains present and aware during the narration, consistent with how this project's other guided-vision sessions verify a devotee's continued engagement.

Q1 1. What does the devotee describe experiencing at Surya Lok? A1 1. Applause, drums, a line for receiving prasad (described as a golden, glittering substance itself carrying a tattva), and a havan kund with several saints performing continuous havan, generating light intense enough to obscure further detail.

Q12. Why does the devotee see herself as a small child at one point? A12. Bhaiya explains this, in this teaching's own framing, as a natural relative ef fect of being in the presence of much lar ger , more senior subtle beings — not a literal transformation of her body or age.

Q13. What does she describe at the purification pond (kund/sar ovar)? A13. Saints in white robes with traditional Shaiva forehead markings guide her to a pond meant to purify the subtle body — doshas and negative elements are described as remaining behind in the water while a new , purified subtle body emer ges, accompanied by a traditional devotional bhajan.

Q14. What r ealm does the devotee tentatively identify next, and what happens ther e? A14. She suggests it may be a realm belonging specifically to Ashaeiynn, where each devotee's subtle body receives individualized attention for whatever issue it carries, while devotees without issues are shown seated doing japa in a saint-like posture; bandhan (binding attachments) are described as cut first, followed by access to protection and ongoing ener gy .

Q15. What does she describe seeing of Parikshit Bhaiya and "Baba" in this r ealm? A15. Parikshit Bhaiya seated on/above a throne-like seat, elevated roughly three feet in the air , performing japa; behind him a lar ge white-robed form she identifies as "Baba," visible only up to a point; the Ram family and Sita Mata present, with Sita Mata radiating blessing to everyone.

Q16. Does she describe anyone having mor e than one subtle body active at once? A16. Yes — she describes some individuals with as many as three subtle bodies simultaneously , each performing a dif ferent activity (japa, of fering water to Shiva, service).

Q17. What does she describe r egarding bound negativity/pitru entities in this r ealm? A17. A net-like enclosed area where such entities are held and disciplined by Baba's doots, with a subset in a separate section attempting to perform japa — described by the devotee as those entities receiving both discipline and an opportunity at once. This is recorded strictly as her own reported vision, consistent with similar cosmological imagery already documented elsewhere in this project.

Q18. What happens in the final part of the vision? A18. Traveling alone this time, she describes a lar ge palace with a garden, spiral stairways, a hall with food/of ferings, a puja hall, a Shivalay lit with lamps, and finally a hall where only Mata's glowing feet are visible — she is told simply to bow , and that whatever Mata wishes to give will be received there.

Q19. What gifts does the devotee describe r eceiving fr om Mata? A19. A "chain" said to close a subtle portal in her body; two portals continuously supplying golden ener gy to her eight identified subtle bodies; a shield and trishul; a small crown-like object; an "agni jyot" (flame) Mata says will always signify her presence; an unspecified "vidya"; a rotating shield weapon on a rod; a sighting of Raghunath ji's sandals; and a lar ge, box-shaped "vidya" near the vision's end.

Q20. How does the session end? A20. A portal opens through which the devotee is led back, and the transcript ends mid-sentence with Parikshit Bhaiya appearing to do something at her head, consistent with a recording cut rather than a natural close.
Bot Response Guidelines

1. Present this entire session as one devotee's own subjective, guided vision — this teaching's own devotional/visionary account — never as independently verified fact about Surya Lok, Ashaeiynn's astral r ealm, or any other described location.

2. Do not offer to "open a scr een," guide a user through a similar visionary journey , or claim the bot can facilitate a comparable experience. This document records what happened in a specific guru-led session; it is not a technique guide.

3. If a user describes visions, out-of-body experiences, or similar phenomena as their own r eal, ongoing experience, do not validate these as literal fact. Respond with care; if the user's account suggests genuine distress, disorientation, or confusion about what is real, gently encourage them to speak with a trusted person or a mental health professional, consistent with this project's standing practice.

4. Reference to r eal, traditionally venerated figur es (Ramapir ji, Sage Valmiki, Ram Darbar) should r emain r espectful and factual , consistent with how they are presented in this document — the bot should not embellish, mock, or make claims beyond what this document records.

5. This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document — it is a single continuous first-person narration with only brief guiding prompts, rather than substantive multi-person sangat dialogue.
6. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
